body.statement: Flagship question: for fixed \(r>1/2\), \(s>0\), and \(0<t\le d/2\), prove or refute the candidate equivalence \(\delta_n^\star\asymp\rho_n^{\mathrm{occ}}\) uniformly over \(c_X\le f_X\le C_X\), where \(\rho_n^{\mathrm{occ}}\) is defined from the primitive cell probabilities, pair-occupancy probabilities, and Gram-inflation factor in \(\mathrm{def{:}occupancy\mbox{-}gram\mbox{-}candidate}\). The lower-bound route must use the explicit nonfactorizing \(q_\omega\) table and shared-sign family \(\{P_\omega,Q_\omega:\omega\in\{-1,1\}^{K_h}\}\) from \(\mathrm{def{:}fuzzy\mbox{-}mixtures}\) at the optimizing scale. Its named obligations are to preserve the exact \(U_{P_\omega}=0\) SCoDiTE null, the nonzero contrast \(U_{Q_\omega}=2u_\omega v_\omega b_Y/(1-u_\omega^2)\), the covariance sandwich and \(0<s\le1/2\) source bound from \(\mathrm{lem{:}fuzzy\mbox{-}legality\mbox{-}affinity}\), and bounded \(n\)-record mixture affinity at the scale selected by the nonuniform cell probabilities. The upper-bound route must either attain this candidate by collision and empirical-Gram calibration or replace it with a rigorously derived primitive occupancy--Gram functional and match that radius. For \(s>1/2\), determine whether covariance-source membership eliminates this fuzzy branch or yields an explicit \((r,s)\)-dependent frontier.
body.justification: This flagship claim turns the rough arbitrary-density bottleneck into a falsifiable rate formula and exposes exact-null legality and covariance-source membership as independent proof obligations.
body.gap: Liu et al. prove their empirical-HOIF efficiency result for scalar missing-at-random and doubly robust functionals with \(k=o(n)\); scales with \(K_h>n\) are therefore not subsumed, but that fact alone neither proves an obstruction nor selects the proposed occupancy factor. No SCoDiTE result supplies the missing lower and upper match.
body.consumer: The matched frontier determines the size-valid detection threshold for the 401(k) conditional wealth-distribution analysis and tells the analyst whether cell occupancy, rather than a heuristic whitening rule, limits sensitivity.

obligation.what_is_open: Whether the all-tests radius equals the proposed occupancy--Gram functional, or another primitive functional, under every density in the fixed band.
obligation.obstruction: The proposed functional evaluates to a rate strictly slower than the legal fuzzy lower bound below the elbow, but the existing paired mixture is controlled by collision likelihood terms proportional to the cell-probability square sum and does not produce the extra Gram-inflation factor. Conversely, the frozen upper handle is not an explicit estimator and supplies no concentration bound.
obligation.attempted: Cell probabilities and pair occupancies were bounded uniformly from the density band, the candidate was optimized on both dense and sparse branches, and the paired likelihood mixture was compared at those scales. These calculations expose rather than close the mismatch.
obligation.partial_result:
The candidate functional itself has a computable rate. The density band gives \(c_X/K_h\le p_{h,j}\le C_X/K_h\). For \(N\sim\operatorname{Binomial}(n,p)\),
\[
P(N\ge2)\asymp\min\{(np)^2,1\}.
\]
The upper bound follows from \(P(N\ge2)\le E[N(N-1)]/2\); for \(np\le1\), the probability of exactly two successes gives the lower bound, and for \(np\ge1\), binomial monotonicity gives a fixed positive lower bound. Hence
\[
\Gamma_n(h;P_X)\asymp
\begin{cases}
1,&K_h\le n,\\
K_h/n,&K_h\ge n.
\end{cases}
\]
For \(0<t\le d/2\), minimizing the sparse expression
\[
K_h^{-t/d}+K_h^{3/2}/n^2
\]
gives \(K_h\asymp n^{4d/(2t+3d)}\ge n\), and therefore
\[
\rho_n^{\mathrm{occ}}\asymp n^{-1/2}\vee n^{-4t/(2t+3d)}.
\]
Dyadic rounding changes only constants. The proved fuzzy construction gives the distinct lower bound \(\delta_n^\star\gtrsim n^{-2t/(2t+d)}\) for \(0<s\le1/2\). When \(t<d/2\), the occupancy candidate is strictly larger because \(4t/(2t+3d)<2t/(2t+d)\); neither an upper estimator nor a matching occupancy lower mixture is supplied.
